events.text: A story is going round the teahouses, and it is about you. In it you beat a master three times your age in a night fight on a bridge nobody else saw. You were not on that bridge. By spring the storytellers have written you onto the Rising Dragons and Phoenixes at {gn_place}, far above anything you have earned.

choices.text: Let them believe it, and enjoy it

effects.log: You do not correct anyone. Strangers buy you dinner. A girl at the inn asks how you held the bridge.

choices.text: Say nothing either way

effects.log: You neither boast nor deny. The story grows on its own, which is what stories do.

choices.text: Tell everyone it never happened

effects.log: You stand up in the teahouse and tell the truth. Half the room thinks you are being modest.

events.text: A herald from the storytellers' guild finds you in the market with a new copy of the Rising Dragons and Phoenixes. Your name is on it at {gn_place}. Underneath, in small brush strokes: "Broke a bandit stronghold alone." You have never seen a bandit stronghold. The herald is waiting, politely, for you to look pleased.

choices.text: Look pleased

effects.log: You look pleased. The herald bows, and by evening the whole market knows the stronghold story.

choices.text: Thank the herald and change the subject

effects.log: You thank the herald and talk about the weather. The list goes up on the market wall all the same.

choices.text: Ask the herald to strike your name off

effects.log: The herald stares at you. Nobody has ever asked that. He promises to tell the guild, and does.

choices.text: Feed the story a little yourself

effects.log: You add a detail or two for the herald to carry. Within a month a merchant pays you to be seen at his shop. (+20 taels)

events.text: Somebody has confused you with somebody else, and the murim has not noticed. The new Rising Dragons and Phoenixes put you at {gn_place}, and young fighters you have never met have started to bow when you pass. One of them asks you, very seriously, to teach him the move you used on the Black Pine Ridge.

choices.text: Show him something, anything

effects.log: You show him the best move you have. He thanks you as if it were a secret. It is not.

choices.text: Tell him to train and stop listening to stories

effects.log: He nods, deeply impressed by your humility. The story only grows.

choices.text: Tell him the truth: you were never there

effects.log: He looks at you a long time, then laughs, and then stops laughing. By the end of the week, the list knows.

events.text: {gn_foe}, of the Rising Dragons and Phoenixes, has heard the story about you, and does not believe a word of it. The challenge is delivered in front of the whole teahouse: tomorrow at dawn, by the old well, with witnesses. If the story is true, it will be easy for you.

choices.text: Go to the well at dawn

effects.log: You go. Half the town is there before you, and so is {gn_foe}, already stretching.

choices.text: Be somewhere else at dawn

effects.log: You are three towns away at dawn. Witnesses wait by the well for an hour, and then go and tell everyone.

choices.text: Go to the well, and tell the truth there

effects.log: You go, and in front of everyone you say that the story was never yours.

events.text: The rumour has carried you a long way, and now it has carried you to a ring of rope in a temple courtyard, where {gn_foe} waits with a borrowed sword and a borrowed crowd. "You are at {gn_place}," {gn_foe} says. "So show me." Somewhere behind you, a storyteller has already wet his brush.

choices.text: Step into the ring

effects.log: You step over the rope. The storyteller leans forward. So does everyone else.

choices.text: Bow out, pleading an old wound

effects.log: You plead an old wound. Nobody in the courtyard believes you have one.

choices.text: Tell them all the rumour is a lie

effects.log: You tell them. The storyteller writes faster than he has ever written before.

events.text: A letter in a careful hand: "Everyone says you are at {gn_place}. Everyone says you beat a master on a bridge. I say you are a story with a face. Meet me at the ferry crossing at the next full moon. {gn_foe}." The ink has gone through the paper in two places.

choices.text: Meet them at the ferry

effects.log: You are at the ferry before the moon is up. So is {gn_foe}, and a boatful of witnesses.

choices.text: Burn the letter and stay home

effects.log: You burn it. {gn_foe} waits at the ferry all night, and tells the ferrymen why.

choices.text: Write back the truth

effects.log: You write back that there was never a bridge. {gn_foe} has the letter copied and posted on every wall.

events.text: The last bout of the Dragons and Phoenixes Tournament ends with you standing, and before the dust has settled the heralds are already arguing about what to call you. By the time the prizes are handed out, they have agreed: the {gn_ep}. Somebody is painting it on a banner. Somebody else is selling copies.

choices.text: Bow to the stands

effects.log: You bow to the stands. They roar the new name back at you: the {gn_ep}.

choices.text: Bow to the one you beat in the final

effects.log: You bow to your last opponent first. The old masters in the stands notice, and nod.

choices.text: Say nothing, and walk out of the ring

effects.log: You walk out without a word. The storytellers decide that is exactly what the {gn_ep} would do.

events.text: An old storyteller with ink on his fingers takes your hand after the final and turns it over, as if reading it. "Path, sect, nature," he says. "The murim names its young by what they are, not by what they want." He writes four words on a strip of paper and gives it to you: the {gn_ep}.

choices.text: Keep the strip of paper

effects.log: You fold it into your sleeve. Years later you still have it: the {gn_ep}.

choices.text: Ask him what he would have called you if you lost

effects.log: "Nothing," he says. "Nobody names the ones who lose. Remember that, and you will keep the name."

events.text: By the next market day you hear it from a stranger at a noodle stall, who does not know who you are: "Did you hear? The {gn_ep} took the Dragons and Phoenixes. They say the final lasted a hundred exchanges." It lasted eleven. The {gn_ep} is you.

choices.text: Let the stranger tell it his way

effects.log: You let him tell it. By the end it has lasted two hundred exchanges, and you are taller.

choices.text: Tell him it was eleven

effects.log: He looks at you, then at your sword, and goes very quiet. Then he pays for your noodles.

events.text: A rider in the blue of the Martial Alliance stops at your door with a letter sealed in white wax. The Alliance Martial Academy, where the young of every righteous house are taught together for four years, invites you to its next term. It says it has heard of you. It does not say from whom.

choices.text: Accept the invitation

effects.log: You write your answer that night: yes. The rider takes it at dawn.

choices.text: Decline it politely

effects.log: You decline. The Academy does not write twice. You train alone, and wonder.

events.text: The letter from the Alliance Martial Academy is short. Four years, it says, among the most promising young fighters under heaven: dormitories, masters, a tournament at the end that the whole murim watches. Below that, one more line in a different hand: "Come. Your generation is waiting to see what you are."

choices.text: Go and find out

effects.log: You pack a bag that night. Four years is a long time. You suspect it will not feel like it.

choices.text: Stay on your own road

effects.log: You put the letter away. Your own road is lonelier, and entirely yours.

events.text: Your name on the Rising Dragons and Phoenixes has reached the Alliance Martial Academy, and the Academy wants its Dragons and Phoenixes inside its walls, where it can watch them. The invitation comes with a jade token and the seal of the Alliance Leader himself.

choices.text: Take the jade token

effects.log: You take the token. Every young name on the list will be there. So will you.

choices.text: Send the token back

effects.log: You send it back. Somewhere in the Alliance, someone writes your name on a different kind of list.

events.text: Four beds, four chests, one window, and three strangers who look at you the way you look at them. {npc} takes the bed by the window without asking, and puts {his} sword across it. "Somebody has to run this room," {he} says to nobody in particular. {gn_room} are watching you to see what you will do.

choices.text: Tell {npc} the room is yours, and prove it

effects.log: You put your own sword on the window bed. {npc} smiles. The yard behind the dormitory is empty at night.

choices.text: Let {npc} have it, and stand behind {him}

effects.log: You nod to {npc}. {He} nods back. In this room, at least, you will never be alone.

choices.text: Take the bed nobody wants and stay out of it

effects.log: You take the bed by the door. From there you can see everyone, which suits you.

events.text: On the first night {npc} lays down the rules of the room: who sweeps, who fetches water, who gets the warm corner in winter. The warm corner, {he} has decided, is {his}. {gn_room} say nothing. Every room in the dormitory is being decided tonight, and every room is listening to every other.

choices.text: Challenge {npc} for the room, in the yard

effects.log: You say it quietly: the yard, now. {npc} is already reaching for {his} boots.

choices.text: Accept the rules, and learn from {npc}

effects.log: You fetch the water. {npc} notices you do it well, and from then on asks your advice.

choices.text: Keep to yourself and watch

effects.log: You watch. Rooms are like sects, you think. Small ones.

choices.text: Inform the room that it is already yours

effects.log: You tell them the room is yours and that they may thank you later. {npc} laughs out loud, and then stops laughing.

events.text: {npc} is the strongest of the four of you and knows it. {He} is not cruel about it, only certain, the way a mountain is certain. {gn_room} have already started calling {him} elder brother or elder sister by turns, half joking. Your first lesson at the Academy, it seems, is about who stands where.

choices.text: Find out if the mountain moves

effects.log: You ask {npc} to spar. {He} raises an eyebrow, and then a hand.

choices.text: Call {him} elder too, and mean it

effects.log: You call {him} elder. {npc} looks surprised, and then pleased, and then protective.

choices.text: Stay friendly with everyone and no one

effects.log: You stay out of it. It costs you nothing yet.

events.text: By the second year the Academy has split, the way a river splits around stones. The stones are its Dragons and Phoenixes, and the young gather around them in cliques that eat together, train together and hate together. {gn_clique} sends someone to sit beside you at dinner. They are your kind of people, the messenger says.

choices.text: Sit with {gn_clique}

effects.log: You move your bowl to their table. They make room as if you had always been there.

choices.text: Go to the strongest clique instead

effects.log: You walk past them to the table of the strongest. Ambition, you tell yourself, is not a crime.

choices.text: Gather your own people

effects.log: The ones from your room follow you to an empty table. By the end of the month, it is not empty.

choices.text: Eat alone

effects.log: You eat alone. The cliques decide you are either very strong or very strange.

events.text: Your old rival is at the Academy too, and in the second year leads {gn_rival_clique}, which has already decided what it thinks of you. Across the yard, {gn_clique} is the opposite of everything your rival stands for, and would love to have you. Everyone is waiting to see which table you choose.

choices.text: Sit with {gn_clique}

effects.log: You sit with {gn_clique}. From across the yard, your rival raises a cup to you, not kindly.

choices.text: Sit with your rival

effects.log: You sit down at your rival's table. The whole yard goes quiet. Your rival, after a long moment, pours you tea.

choices.text: Gather your own people

effects.log: You start a third table. Your rival looks at it, and at you, and understands this is a declaration.

choices.text: Belong to nobody

effects.log: You belong to nobody. Both tables watch you more than they watch each other.

events.text: Two Dragons of {gn_gen} share a clique this year, and a Phoenix leads the next, and nobody can agree which of them is strongest. Each clique has its colours, its corner of the training yard, its songs. {gn_clique} has been watching you train for a month, and tonight leaves a ribbon of its colour on your bed.

choices.text: Tie on the ribbon of {gn_clique}

effects.log: You tie it on. In the morning you have twenty friends and three new enemies.

choices.text: Take it to the strongest clique and offer your sword

effects.log: You throw the ribbon away and go to the strongest. They test you, and keep you.

choices.text: Make a ribbon of your own

effects.log: You dye a ribbon of a colour nobody has chosen. By spring, a dozen others wear it.

choices.text: Leave the ribbon on the bed

effects.log: You leave it there. It is still there at graduation, faded.

events.text: {npc} trips you in front of the masters' hall and laughs while you get up. It is the third time this month. Inside these walls nobody may kill, or be killed: the Academy's first law, carved over the gate. {npc} knows it, and leans on it like a staff.

choices.text: Swallow it, and remember

effects.log: You get up, dust yourself off and remember the face. The Academy has walls. The world does not.

choices.text: Challenge {npc} to a sanctioned bout

effects.log: You ask the masters for a bout, by the rules, in the yard. {npc} accepts, grinning.

choices.text: Report {him} to the masters

effects.log: You report it. {npc} sweeps the masters' hall for a month, and will not forget who put {him} there.

choices.text: Break the law, and finish it

effects.log: Something in you snaps. You go for {his} throat, and the whole yard sees it.

events.text: Someone has torn the pages of your manual and left them in the well, and everyone knows it was {npc}, and nobody can prove it. {He} meets your eyes across the yard and smiles. Kill {him} and the Academy expels you. Leave it and it will follow you out of the gate.

choices.text: Leave it for the day you graduate

effects.log: You copy the manual out again, page by page. Every page, you think of {npc}.

choices.text: Beat {him} in a bout, inside the rules

effects.log: You name the bout in front of the whole Academy. {npc} cannot refuse it without losing face.

choices.text: Take it to the masters, without proof

effects.log: The masters listen, and believe you, and can do nothing. {npc} finds out you went to them.

choices.text: Wait for {him} behind the kitchens with a blade

effects.log: You wait behind the kitchens. When {npc} comes, you are not thinking about the law at all.

events.text: {npc} of another clique has made you the target of the year: rumours, a broken practice sword, a laugh in every corridor you walk down. Inside the Academy you cannot touch {him} with intent to kill. Outside, after graduation, there will be no walls between you.

choices.text: Let the grudge wait for the gate

effects.log: You let it wait. Patience, you find, can be sharpened like anything else.

choices.text: Answer {him} in the sanctioned ring

effects.log: You answer in the ring, by the rules, with the masters watching.

choices.text: Smile at {him}, every day, until it frightens {him}

effects.log: You smile at {npc} every morning. By winter, {he} has started to sleep with a knife.

choices.text: End {him} in the night

effects.log: You go to {his} room in the night. The Academy's first law is carved over the gate, and you walk under it anyway.

events.text: The last tournament of the Alliance Martial Academy. The Alliance Leader sits under a white canopy; behind him, the heads of every great house have come to see their young. Whoever wins today is the {gn_title} of {gn_gen}, and will be called it for the rest of their life.

choices.text: Fight for the crown with everything you have

effects.log: You step into the ring. The drums start. Four years, and it comes down to this afternoon.

choices.text: Fight, and yield before it turns ugly

effects.log: You fight well, and when it is clear it could go either way, you step back and bow. The masters see it.

events.text: Four years of rooms, cliques and grudges, and now one ring. The cliques sit in their colours around it, shouting their Dragons' names and their Phoenixes'. The heralds have two crowns ready, one for the {gn_title} of {gn_gen}, and they do not yet know whose head it is for.

choices.text: Go for the crown

effects.log: You go for it. The noise of the cliques falls away until there is only the ring.

choices.text: Let someone else have it

effects.log: You let it go. Some crowns are heavier than they look.

events.text: The gate of the Alliance Martial Academy stands open for the graduates. Outside, the recruiters of the Alliance's armies have set up their tables in the road: the Blue Dragon Army, the Azure Army, the White Tiger Guard. Behind you, the ones who followed you for four years are waiting to see which way you turn.

choices.text: Sign with {gn_army}

effects.log: You walk to the recruiters' tables with your head up.

choices.text: Take your followers home with you

effects.log: You turn to the ones who followed you. "Come home with me," you say. They do not need to be asked twice.

choices.text: Walk past every table

effects.log: You walk past the tables and down the road, owing nobody.

events.text: On the last morning the masters ring the gate bell once for every graduate. When yours sounds, you walk out into a road full of banners. An officer of the Azure Army falls into step beside you. "The Alliance needs young officers," she says. "And you, I think, need something to do with all that."

choices.text: Take her offer

effects.log: You take it. She hands you a token and tells you where to report.

choices.text: Tell her your people come with you, wherever you go

effects.log: You nod at the ones behind you. The officer counts them, and understands you are not a recruit. You are a house.

choices.text: Thank her and go your own way

effects.log: You thank her. She shrugs: the road is long, and the Alliance will still be there.

events.text: {npc} is waiting for you at a crossroads with {his} sword already drawn. "There are no walls here," {he} says. "No masters, no laws over the gate. Just you, and me, and four years I have not forgotten."

choices.text: Settle it, and leave {him} alive

effects.log: You draw. Four years of grudge come down to a crossroads in the rain.

choices.text: Settle it for good

effects.log: You draw, and this time nobody is coming to pull you apart.

choices.text: Lower your sword and forgive {him}

effects.log: You sheathe your sword. {npc} stares at you as if you had struck {him}.

choices.text: Walk around {him}

effects.log: You walk around {him}. "Another year, then," {npc} says to your back.

events.text: A letter in a hand you have not seen since the Academy: "You remember me. I remember you. The old law does not hold outside the gate. The bamboo grove by the river, at the new moon. {npc}." The paper smells faintly of the Academy's ink.

choices.text: Go to the grove and settle it

effects.log: You go. The bamboo creaks in the dark like a door left open.

choices.text: Go to the grove and end it

effects.log: You go with your blade loose in its sheath, and no intention of coming back with a grudge.

choices.text: Write back that it is over

effects.log: You write that it is over, for you. {npc} reads it twice and then, slowly, believes it.

choices.text: Do not answer

effects.log: You do not answer. {npc} waits in the grove until dawn.

events.text: Years have passed since the Academy, and {npc} has not let one of them go by without thinking of you. Now {he} has found you in a crowded inn, and the whole room can feel it. "Outside," {he} says. "We were never allowed to finish it in there."

choices.text: Step outside and finish it

effects.log: You step outside. The inn empties behind you to watch.

choices.text: Step outside, and make it the last time

effects.log: You step outside, and something in your face makes the watchers stand back further.

choices.text: Buy {him} a drink instead

effects.log: You pour {npc} a cup. {He} looks at it for a long time before {he} drinks.

choices.text: Finish your meal and leave by the back

effects.log: You leave by the back. {npc} will find you again. {He} always does.
